title: Highest-Protein Seeds: Ranking per 100 Grams and per Ounce

seo.title: Highest-Protein Seeds per Serving
seo.meta_description: Compare hemp, pumpkin, sunflower, flax, sesame and chia by protein per 100 grams and per 1-ounce serving.
seo.search_intent: Compare edible seeds by protein concentration and serving.

excerpt: Hulled hemp and pumpkin seeds contain around 30 g protein per 100 g. A 1-ounce serving provides roughly 8–9 g.
content_html:
Seeds are concentrated foods with little water and substantial protein, fat, fiber and minerals. Per 100 grams they can approach lean meat, but a normal serving is usually 1–2 tablespoons or about 1 ounce.

Protein ranking

SeedProtein/100 gProtein/1 oz
Hulled hemp31.6 g8.8 g
Pumpkin kernels30.2 g8.5 g
Sunflower kernels20.8 g5.8 g
Flaxseed18.3 g5.1 g
Sesame17.7 g5.0 g
Chia16.5 g4.6 g

Hemp and pumpkin

Hulled hemp provides 31.6 g protein/100 g and pumpkin seeds 30.2 g, close to cooked chicken breast at about 31 g/100 g.

Serving size changes the comparison: 1 ounce of hemp gives about 8.8 g protein, while a 5-ounce chicken breast provides about 44 g.

Sunflower

Sunflower kernels contain about 20.8 g protein/100 g and nearly 6 g per ounce, along with vitamin E, copper and unsaturated fat.

Flax and chia

Flax is about 18.3 g protein/100 g and chia about 16.5 g. Chia stands out even more for fiber at roughly 34 g/100 g, with flax around 27 g.

A 20 g serving of chia supplies about 3.3 g protein and 6.8 g fiber; flax provides about 3.7 g protein and 5.4 g fiber.

Sesame

Sesame seeds contain about 17.7 g protein/100 g. Tahini retains a substantial amount of that protein, although brands differ with roasting and added ingredients.

Calories

Most seeds exceed 500 calories/100 g because they are rich in fat. Hemp is around 550 calories with 31.6 g protein, compared with cooked chicken breast at about 165 calories with 31 g. Similar protein by weight does not mean similar calorie density.

How to use them

A 1-ounce serving can add 5–9 g protein to oatmeal, yogurt, salads or sauces. Seeds work especially well as a protein supplement to meals already built around legumes, tofu or other foods.

Bottom line

Hemp and pumpkin seeds lead on protein concentration. Sunflower, flax, sesame and chia provide less protein but bring other strengths such as fiber, vitamin E, magnesium and unsaturated fats.

Sources

Values come from USDA FoodData Central.

faq.question: Which seed has the most protein?
faq.answer: Hulled hemp is about 31.6 g/100 g and pumpkin seeds about 30.2 g/100 g.

faq.question: How much protein is in one ounce of seeds?
faq.answer: Hemp provides about 8.8 g, pumpkin 8.5 g and sunflower about 5.8 g.

faq.question: Is chia high in protein?
faq.answer: It contains about 16.5 g/100 g and is even more notable for fiber at roughly 34 g/100 g.
